- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true price shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50% of 30d moving avg), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent trend reversal.  
- For 30d horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; if sentiment shifts sharply, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment change.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., 0.33, 1.00, 0.33), model may overfit short-term noise; apply smoothing filter or reduce volatility weight in forecast.
